posts.name: phantaskippy
posts.cooked:
Problems with Visionary.

1.  Late 2000's project Cocoon starts.

2.  2018 she travels back in time to the present, where she is 17.

3.  Travels Back In Time.  Not travels to a different dimension.

4.  Further the Late 2000s is when the political situation starts with rumors of nuclear testing.  When they announce their nuclear stockpile project Cocoon is started.  You don't go from tests to stockpile in a few days, that takes time.  Then the response is engineering soldiers, which starts with active troops and moves to Project Cocoon. Visionary should be 6-10 at most in 2018.  

5.  She transports back to "Our Present" which gives a norrow range of years, and comes back to save "her infant self."  The game was released in 2011, or roughly when Cocoon was occuring, so that time makes sense.  2018 needs to be 2028 for the timing to work.  Otherwise WTH?

 

We have a few options to work this out.

1.  Visionary's timeline was first, and her presence after coming back created what we know as the main timeline.  The main timeline already involves a from-the-future Visionary, so it would make sense that the main timeline wouldn't have to be the original.  The Trap that is key to the 3 possibilities doesn't happen till after Vengeance, so she had plenty of time to change that event, even unwittingly.  That trap hasn't occured yet in the card game, it happens after the Dreamer and Shattered Timelines.  It is an event that affected them before it happened because of the shattering.  It is quite possible that the varianc in the possibilities is due to the Visionary being present.

2.  Visionary not only crossed time but entered a different dimension, which would be irrelevant because she went before the key events that would create her timeline differences transpired.   The late 2000's happening differently doesn't work, because we have The Dreamer.  Visionary can't save her younger self in a reality where she doesn't even exist.  Project Cocoon has to happen.  Besides.look at fixed point.  It doesn't make sense that she enters a timeline where the point of creating Iron Legacy has passed, because she's around a long time before that trap, and it is the result of the trap that makes the big changes.

 

Basically my argument is that The base storyline we consider the original timeline was already affected by The Visionary's presence.  Her being there changed what would happen, basically her trip succeeded at stopping Iron Legacy from occuring, intentionally or not.

Of course I also think The Visionary is the reason the Time Cataclysm occurs.  Either her, her younger self, or a combinatino of them.

I hold to the theorem that Visionary's temporal jaunt actually created a new universe. If one subscribes to a certain brand of multiverse theory, that may well be the only way to travel in time.

Logically speaking, this pretty much has to be true.  For anyone who doesn't travel in a police box, temporal paradoxes are just a dead stop to any attempt at conceptualizing traveling back in time within your own history.  I mean, "the butterfly effect" isn't just a fuzzy conceptualization - the moment you stepped out into the past, the air you exhaled would have bacteria in it which had survived a few generations of battling with your immune system, and those would now be in the past, spawning new generations of offspring that were more resistant.  You couldn't possibly not alter your history enough to create a paradox; just physically occupying a space that was previously empty would alter too many molecular-level interactions for the result not to affect your future self.  And those alterations would be compounded when your future self traveled back in time just as you originally did, and then they'd compound again and again until the results were macroscopic, and catastropic.  At which point, once you've killed your future self, he no longer travels back in time and the entire thing didn't happen.  So there's just no possible way.  There is simply no part of the universe that isn't connected to the gigantic clockwork mechanism which is "all matter and energy ever"; nothing can ever not affect all other things to a microscopic extent, and those changes inevitably add up.
